The 'sinking of U-352' was a naval action of the Second Happy Time. On 9 May 1942, USCGC Icarus sank the German submarine U-352 off the Outer Banks of North Carolina.
Background
Action
On 9 May, Icarus set off into the waters off Cape Lookout, the southernmost point of the Core Banks. She was commanded by Lieutenant Edward D. Howard. The cutter's communications officer sent a message to the commandant of the Sixth Naval District to inform him that they had entered the region, and got a cold "Received" in reply. The day was warm and overcast, with an almost flat seavisibility was . Icarus was traveling at a speed of  with a southwest heading.
At 1620, a contact was made by the cutter's sonar. The contact was detected off the port bow; it was then reported to the pilothouse. No vessel could be seen on the surface, and Howard decided not to call for general quarters. The object was moving slower than Icarus but on a parallel course. Five minutes later, the contact suddenly improved as the cutter began to overtake the object. Howard then called Lieutenant Maurice Jester to the bridge. At 1629, an explosion from the port quarter of the cutter rocked her; general quarters was sounded, and Jester was given command of the ship. Howard suspected that a torpedo had missed Icarus but struck the seabed. A swirl of mud and water was visible about  off the cutter's port quarter.
